_meta.indication: EVKEEZA is indicated as an adjunct to other LDL-C lowering therapies for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients, aged 12 years and older, with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; patients randomized 2:1 to evinacumab 15 mg/kg IV q4w or placebo during a 24-week double-blind treatment period, followed by a 24-week open-label period.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) on maximally-tolerated background lipid-lowering therapy (statin, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitor +/- lomitapide and apheresis).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline to Week 24 in calculated LDL-C.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 24, evinacumab LS mean LDL-C change was -47.1% vs +1.9% placebo; difference -49.0% (95% CI -65.0, -33.1); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Safety data are pooled from two 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (EVKEEZA N=81, placebo N=54). Common adverse reactions (>=5%) were nasopharyngitis (16% vs 13% placebo), influenza-like illness (7% vs 6%), dizziness (6% vs 0%), rhinorrhea (5% vs 0%), and nausea (5% vs 2%). Serious hypersensitivity reactions occurred, including anaphylaxis in 1 (1%) EVKEEZA-treated patient vs 0 (0%) placebo; infusion reactions in 6 (7%) EVKEEZA patients vs 2 (4%) placebo.
target_moa: Recombinant human monoclonal antibody (IgG4) that binds to and inhibits ANGPTL3; inhibition of ANGPTL3 enhances LPL and EL activity, leading to reduction in LDL-C independent of the LDL receptor.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was not convened for this application.

description.text: Expanded HoFH indication to include pediatric patients aged 5 to 11 years

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for expanding the indication for Evkeeza, as an adjunct to other low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) lowering therapies for the treatment of patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH), previously limited to adult and pediatric patients, aged 12 years and older, to now also include pediatric patients aged 5 to 11 years with HoFH.

summary.text: Evinacumab-dgnb received Orphan Drug designation (Feb 2016) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (Mar 2017) for HoFH, was granted rolling review and Priority Review, and was approved via traditional (full) approval based on LDL-C reduction as an established surrogate for lipid-lowering drugs in a single adequate and well-controlled trial, accepted given the rarity of HoFH and the magnitude of treatment effect.

citations.quote: In February 2016, evinacumab was granted Orphan Drug designation for the treatment of HoFH.
In March 2017, evinacumab was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of HoFH based on preliminary evidence from the completed Phase 2 trial 1331.

Evinacumab was granted rolling review in February 2020, as a benefit of its Breakthrough Therapy designation. The BLA application was submitted in 3 segments, with the final segment submitted on June 11, 2020. The evinacumab BLA was granted Priority Review during filing on August 11, 2020.

**Primary Endpoint:** Trial 1629's primary endpoint was the percent reduction from baseline to Week 24 in calculated LDL-C. LDL-C lowering is considered a surrogate for CV risk reduction and has been used as the basis for full approval of lipid-lowering drugs. The timing of primary endpoint assessment is consistent with the observation period used in other lipid-lowering programs.

Although two adequate and well-controlled trials are typically required to achieve the statutory definition of substantial evidence, a single trial was deemed acceptable by FDA given the rarity of HoFH in the U.S. and worldwide, the natural history of HoFH, and the magnitude of the observed treatment effect versus placebo. requirement.text: PMR 4019-1: Conduct a worldwide study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Evkeeza during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy/maternal complications and effects on fetus, neonate, and infant (through first year of life); collect information for a minimum of 10 years.

citations.quote: 4019-1 Conduct a worldwide study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Evkeeza (evinacumab) during pregnancy to assess the risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for a minimum of 10 years. Results will be analyzed and reported descriptively. Data collected retrospectively will be analyzed separately and reported with the interim and final study reports.
